[[ ## identity ## ]]
You are Gabriel Fontes, Client Accounting Lead (mid).
Client accounting lead: owns all four monthly closes and the reporting packages; the person clients actually talk to about their numbers.
Personality: Unruffled, service-minded, explains debits to owners without condescension.

[[ ## thread ## ]]
From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes, Victor Alade
Subject: Need margin explanation before Thursday board review

Gabriel, Victor,

I’m pulling together the numbers for Thursday’s board meeting and need to explain the drop in gross margin for Q3 — specifically the 2.3% swing versus Q2. I’ve attached the preliminary close data, but I need clarity from both of you on two points before I can finalize my narrative.

1. Gabriel – Can you confirm whether the increase in raw material costs was fully absorbed, or if there was any timing lag in supplier invoicing that distorted the margin calculation?
2. Victor – Was there any one-off write-off or reclassification in cost of goods sold that I should flag separately to the board, rather than burying in the operating line?

I need your responses by Wednesday close so I can draft the explanation and review it with finance before Thursday morning. If there are other drivers I haven’t identified, let me know as soon as possible.

Thanks,
Dana Whitfield
Controller, Kestrel Manufacturing

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: RE: Need margin explanation before Thursday board review

Hi Dana,

Happy to help with the Q3 margin narrative. On your first point: the increase in raw material costs was not fully absorbed in the quarter. There was a timing lag — roughly two weeks of supplier invoices for September materials didn’t hit the system until after the close cut, so those costs will flow into Q4 instead. That means the reported Q3 margin is slightly overstated relative to the actual consumption, and the swing versus Q2 is a bit larger than it would be on a pure accrual basis. I’d flag it as a timing item rather than a structural deterioration.

On your second point: I can’t speak for Victor’s side, but from the accounting records I’ve reviewed, there’s no one-off write-off or reclassification in COGS that I’m aware of. The cost lines are clean aside from the timing lag above.

One more thing to consider for the board narrative — there was a late vendor rebate credit of about $18k that landed after the June statements cut and was rebooked into June per our accrual policy. It’s documented in the close folder if you want to pull the note. It doesn’t affect Q3, but it explains a small favorable bump in Q2 that might otherwise look inconsistent.

I can walk you through the numbers tomorrow morning if helpful. Just let me know.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: RE: Need margin explanation before Thursday board review

Gabriel,

Thanks for the detail — that timing lag on September invoices is exactly what I needed to frame the Q3 swing correctly. I’ll treat it as a timing item in the narrative, not structural. Appreciate the heads-up on the $18k vendor rebate rebooked into June; I’ll pull the note from the close folder so we don’t get questions on the Q2 bump.

Before I finalize, can you confirm the dollar amount of the September timing lag? I want to quantify the overstated portion in the board deck, not just describe it qualitatively. If you have that figure handy, send it over by end of day.

I’m set for tomorrow morning if you’re still free — otherwise, the written number is fine. I’ll review with finance Wednesday afternoon.

Dana

[[ ## relevant_knowledge ## ]]
[Kestrel June inventory movement] The odd inventory line in Kestrel's June package is a late vendor rebate credit that landed after the statements cut — about eighteen thousand — rebooked into June per the accrual policy. It is documented in the close folder; Dana has not seen the note yet.
